purpose: Palynziq is used to lower the levels of phenylalanine (an amino acid) in the blood of adults who have phenylketonuria (PKU). PKU is a rare genetic condition where the body cannot break down phenylalanine properly, causing it to build up to harmful levels. This medicine helps manage PKU in adults whose phenylalanine levels are not well controlled by diet or other treatments alone.
how_it_works: Your body normally uses an enzyme to break down phenylalanine from the food you eat, but in PKU that enzyme does not work correctly. Palynziq is an engineered enzyme (originally from a bacteria) that works in a different way to help break down phenylalanine in your blood. By doing this job, it helps reduce phenylalanine to safer levels in your body.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include injection site reactions (redness, swelling, pain, or itching where the shot is given), joint pain, fatigue (tiredness), nausea, headache, skin rash, dizziness, and stomach pain. Allergic reactions are also very common with this medicine.
warnings: Palynziq can cause serious allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis (a life-threatening reaction), especially when starting or increasing your dose. Because of this risk, you must carry an epinephrine auto-injector (like an EpiPen) with you at all times and know how to use it. This medicine is only available through a special program called the Palynziq REMS Program, which means your doctor must enroll you before prescribing it. Tell your doctor right away if you have trouble breathing, swelling of the face or throat, rapid heartbeat, or feel faint after your injection.
typical_dosing: Palynziq is given as a shot under the skin (subcutaneous injection), usually self-injected at home. Your doctor will start you on a low dose of 2.5 mg once a week and very slowly increase the dose over many months to help your body get used to it. The target maintenance dose is typically 20 mg once daily, but your doctor will personalize the schedule based on how your body responds and tolerates the medicine.
